newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia to increase state's stake in Cimos.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia to increase state's stake in Cimos.

text.p: The Slovenian government said on Thursday it would increase its stake in troubled car parts maker Cimos to about 85 percent from 77 percent currently.
"The government will exchange 80 percent of its outstanding claims towards Cimos for an ownership share," Metod Dragonja, Minister of Economic Activities, told a news conference.
He added the government would reschedule Cimos' remaining debt and that the company was expected to conclude a similar rescheduling agreement with commercial creditors.
Out of Cimos' total debt of 24.6 billion tolars ($170 million), the company owes 2.5 billion tolars to the state.
Cimos is 1.4 billion in debt to Citroen and has agreed it will be repaid over 10 years.

Cimos, which was established in 1972, has faced ongoing financial problems since Slovenia's independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, when the company lost about half of its production capacities which were located in Croatia.
The situation deteriorated over the following years, when Cimos was forced to take on loans at steep interest rates to finance an overhaul of its production lines.
